data.narrative:
Phoenix Tailings is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Nick Myers, Tomás Villalón, and Anthony Balladon. The company has raised $117.8M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 comparable companies across climate and energy, comprising 1 public company and 8 private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $118M in total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying a $224M valuation. Peer-median benchmarking across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C)—yields a $1.0B median with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

The two methods triangulate to a valuation range of $190M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $612M. The gap between stage-progression and peer-median reflects the typical dispersion in early-stage climate tech valuations and uncertainty around Phoenix Tailings' relative competitive positioning within its peer cohort. Key uncertainties include technology maturity, capital efficiency relative to named peers, and market timing for the next financing round. The wide peer range ($700M–$3.0B) underscores sector heterogeneity and the sensitivity of valuation to individual company execution metrics not captured in this stage-based analysis.
